mizutani: capital unknown; possibly Begram on the Logar river 10 km SE of Kabul (水野) (uncertain)

basis: Mizutani's Begram on the Logar near Kabul lies outside Lampaka as bounded by Cunningham/Beal (N of Kabul river, Alingar–Kunar); Vivien's site is the only one inside; no gazetteer; Foucher I p. 150: large mounds near Mandrawar (Alexander's Nikaia), Buddhist foundations at the Alingar-Alishang confluence; no capital named

mizutani: Dasht-i-Begrām near Chahār-bāgh, SW of Jalālābād, S bank of the Kabul river; 慈恩伝 calls it 燃燈城 (Dīpavatī) (agreed)
proposed: Begram/Dasht-i-Begram W/SW of Jalalabad
basis: Cunningham, Vivien agree; Simpson's Surkhab–Kabul junction site (Beal, Watters tentative, Majumdar reports) unresolved; no gazetteer; Foucher I p. 152: fixed from Hadda and the Syah-sang shadow cave, SW suburb of Jalalabad where tradition keeps a Begram; not Simpson's confluence (provisional)

mizutani: possibly the Ahin-Pōsh stūpa E of the old city of Jalālābād (樋口) (uncertain)
proposed: Ahin-Posh stupa (Foucher 1923, Higuchi), or Nagara Goondee tope (Watters, after Masson/Simpson)
basis: depends on the capital; Foucher I p. 152: Life's SE fits from Begram, dome over 75 m round, Simpson's coins (Domitian, Trajan, early Kushan) show 2nd-c. rebuilding (working hypothesis); no gazetteer

mizutani: Gopāla's cave: among the Syāh-sang rocks S of Chahār-bāgh village, along the cliffs S of Jalālābād; which cave exactly cannot be told (樋口) (uncertain)
proposed: cliffs S/SW of Jalalabad (Syah-sang); exact cave unknown
basis: Watters places it in the same range; no gazetteer; Foucher I p. 152: Faxian, Songyun, Xuanzang lead to the Syah-sang gap; c. 6 monasteries and 12 stupas within 500 m; cave lost in the conglomerate

mizutani: — (unknown)
proposed: immediately N of Shah-ji-ki-Dheri, c. 1.5 miles SE of Peshawar, where a small octagonal Hindu temple now stands (Spooner); tree perished (Babur 1505 saw it, Abul Fazl 1594 silent)
basis: ASR II pp. 88-89 (Cunningham): Babur 1505, Abul Fazl 1594 silent; Spooner AR 1908-09 (after Foucher): tree not to be found, small octagonal Hindu temple N of Shah-ji-ki-Dheri where it should stand; Peshawar 1883/1899 echo ASR II; follows from 02.04.03

mizutani: Shāh-ji-ki-Dheri, c. 1 km SE of Peshawar (the 雀離浮図 of 宋雲); excavated by Spooner 1908–09 (agreed)
proposed: Shah-ji-ki-Dheri
basis: Spooner AR 1908-09 pp. 48-53: relic chamber of the E mound, bronze casket inscribed 'Kanishka's vihara in the sangharama of Mahasena', crystal reliquary with bones, coin of Kanishka; AR 1909-10 casket with Kanishka's figure and name; Hargreaves AR 1910-11 cruciform base 180 ft; Vogel's note: 1875 Sappers' dig, Cunningham's unpublished shift to the site; ASR II p. 89 'no remains' was hearsay; Thana 1882 footnote 'perhaps Manikyala' unargued; Konow CII 2.1 pp. 135-138 re-reads the casket (year 1 of Kanishka, Kanishka's vihara in Mahasena's sangharama, Sarvastivadin teachers), site "proved to be correct"

mizutani: possibly Gor Khattri at the NE corner of Peshawar city (uncertain)
proposed: the great W mound beside Kanishka's stupa at Shah-ji-ki-Dheri (Spooner), not Gor Khatri
basis: Spooner AR 1908-09: W mound = monastic quadrangle W of the stupa as in the text; casket inscription (AR 1909-10) names the Vihara of Kanishka in the Mahasena monastery, monastery 'portions of which we have now recovered'; Hargreaves AR 1910-11 monastery wall facing the stupa; Vogel: Gor Katri was Cunningham's published first conjecture (ASR II p. 89), later dropped by him; Peshawar 1883/1899 echo ASR II

mizutani: Chārsadda, left bank of the Swat river a little above its confluence with the Kabul river, 17 miles from Peshawar (agreed)
proposed: Charsadda/Prang (Hashtnagar)
basis: Garrick ASR XIX pp. 101-104 surveyed the Bala Hissar mound and its gates; Cunningham ASR II pp. 89-90 (100 li of the Life); Majumdar (excavated); Peshawar 1883/1899 echo; Vivien's Nisatta superseded; Pargiter EI 12 p. 302, Konow CII 2.1 pp. 117-118: Hashtnagar pedestal (year 384), Hashtnagar villages on the site of Pushkalavati; Marshall and Vogel 1903 Palatu Dheri excavation near Rajar (Buddhist monument, late Kushan coins); no record names the town

proposed: Mekha-Sanda (hills NE of Shahbaz Garhi)
basis: Hargreaves AR 1922-23 p. 17: faint foundations on the Mekha-Sanda hill NE of Shahbazgarhi 'mark the retreat of the exiled prince'; Majumdar's double cave NE of the edicts in the same hills; Cunningham's Kashmiri-ghar/Kashmir Smast (ASR II pp. 91-92; Peshawar 1883/1899 repeat) fixed from his own abandoned Palodheri

mizutani: Ohind (Hund, Und), NE of the Indus–Kabul confluence, 16 miles above Attock (agreed)
proposed: Hund (Ohind) on the Indus
basis: Hargreaves AR 1923-24 pp. 68-69: diaper walls under the Muslim fort, Gandhara walling, probable stupa base, 3rd-5th c. remains, 20 li circuit plausible as the Indus has cut away the S side; Cunningham ASR II pp. 92-95 (name history, coins); Vivien, Cunningham, Beal, Majumdar agree; Watters' doubt unsupported; Himalayan Districts II 1884 and 1874 volume repeat; Sahni EI 22 pp. 97-98: 8th-c. Sarada temple slab found at Hund (Cobb), mounds, Indo-Greek to Shahi coins, unexcavated; Sircar EI 35: Udabhanda = Und; no record names the town

mizutani: Taxila, 21 miles NW of Rawalpindi (agreed)
proposed: Taxila ruins near Shah-dheri/Sarai-kala
basis: three inscriptions naming Taksasila found on the site: copper plate at Thupkia in Sirsukh (ASR V pp. 67-68; Rawalpindi 1883/1895), silver scroll at the Dharmarajika (Marshall AR 1913-14 pp. 12-13), ladle 'Tachhasilae' from the Sirkap Mahal (AR 1923-24); Cunningham found the site 1863 (ASR II p. 85); Vivien's Hasan Abdal superseded; Konow CII 2.1 pp. 23-29, 87, EI 14; Buhler EI 4 pp. 54-55: Patika plate "in the town of Takshasila", Sihila vase from mound 13 near the Chir Tope "in Takshasila", two Mahal ladles, Dharmarajika scroll: four inscriptions found on the site

mizutani: Sirsukh (the third, Kushan-period city NNE of Sirkap), not Bhir Mound or Sirkap (agreed)
proposed: Sirsukh (Marshall)
basis: Marshall AR 1915-16 pp. 11-14: SE corner of Sirsukh fortifications in Kushan large-diaper masonry, round loopholed bastions, 3rd-4th c. block in the centre (no 7th-c. occupation shown); Cunningham's Bir mound (ASR II pp. 117-118: coins, lapis, distance to his head-gift stupa, which Marshall moved to Bhallar; Rawalpindi 1883/1895 echo) is surface evidence; Patika plate: Konow CII 2.1 p. 26 Saka city = Sirkap, Buhler EI 4 p. 54 Takhasila = Sirsukh; both 1st c., not decisive for the 7th

mizutani: ruined stūpa on the ridge above Baoti Pind (agreed)
proposed: the stupa on the NE peak of the Baoti ridge above Baoti Pind
basis: Cunningham ASR II pp. 139-140: stupa 65 ft diam. with monastery, excavated (relic chamber, earthenware vessel), Langar-kot fort; Rawalpindi 1883/1895, Attock 1909 echo; requires reading E for SE; nothing names the place

proposed: Bhallar stupa, Sarda hill (Marshall)
basis: Marshall AR 1915-16 pp. 3-4 identifies Bhalar with the 'Sacrificed Head' (no argument given; terrace and monastery uncleared); AR 1912-13 p. 16: Cunningham's Jhandiala stupa is 3rd c. over a Scytho-Parthian one, but AR 1914-15 p. 13 makes Bhalar 3rd c. too; Cunningham's Babar-khana (ASR II pp. 114-121; ASR V p. 72) measured from the Bir mound; Sirsukh at the NE corner of Babar-khana

mizutani: Marshall: on the N slope of the W end of the Hathiāl ridge S of Sirkap, beside the Kunāla monastery (disputed)
proposed: large stupa on the plateau N of the Hathial ridge, with monastery (Marshall, excavated)
basis: Marshall AR 1914-15 pp. 13-14: excavated three-tiered base 63 x 105 ft, 3rd-c. stupa over a 1st-c. memorial stupa, monastery beside; no inscription; Yamamoto: from Sirsukh the bearing SE fails (unanswered); Cunningham's Karmal (ASR II pp. 149-150, nothing found; Rawalpindi 1883/1895 quote) and Meri hill (ASR XIV, bearing E) both measured from the Bir mound; Boyer (via Konow EI 14 p. 287): Kunala stupa = the Dharmarajika (Chir Tope), from the word dharmarajika only, undecided by Konow; scroll does not name Kunala

mizutani: Ketās (Ketāksh, Khetās), N of the Salt Range, 16 miles from Pind Dadan Khan on the Jhelum (32°43′N, 72°59′E) (agreed)
proposed: Ketas locality, Salt Range
basis: Cunningham: Malot (ASR II pp. 191-192) -> Ketas (AGI 1871) -> Malot (ASR V p. 85, routes marched), 9 miles apart in the same Salt Range; Jhelam 1907 prints Stein's field evidence (forts, stupa, Murti) against Malot; Buhler concurs; Dehra Dun 1911 attests the kingdom; Buhler EI 1 pp. 11-12: Lakkha Mandal prasasti (Dehra Dun, c. 600) names the Yadava kings of Singhapura = Sang-ho-pu-lo; name only, found far E

mizutani: Kotera, ruined fort on the hill overlooking Ketās (Cunningham, by emending 4.3's 四五十里 to 四五里) (uncertain)
proposed: field of ruins on the plain 1-2 miles N of Ketas (Stein); rival Malot hill-fort (Cunningham ASR II, V); not Kotera
basis: Kotera (AGI) needs 4-5 li for 40-50 and was abandoned by Cunningham in both reports for Malot (ASR V p. 85: high mountain, distance unemended); Jhelam 1907 (Stein): 40-50 li NW of Murti; both rivals keep the text

mizutani: large base, probably of a stūpa, at the foot of the Kotera hill, with a Kashmiri-style temple of the 9th–14th c. in front (Majumdar) (uncertain)
proposed: large stupa before the E front of the Sat-Ghara temples, Ketas
basis: Jhelam 1907 (Stein): Asoka stupa before the E front of the Sat-Ghara temples, apparently the basement Majumdar describes; Cunningham ASR V p. 92 read the early basement C there as the Jaina temple, and (p. 90) found nothing S of Malot

proposed: Murti mound in the Gandhala valley (Stein)
basis: Jhelam 1907 (Stein): excavated true stupa, 30+ camel-loads of Jaina sculpture, pools with fish and trees, local Jaina tradition, chained 4.5 miles; Buhler accepted; Watters reserved; but Cunningham ASR V pp. 90-92 counted seven walled pools at Ketas, a rocky spur and a ruined monastery 400 ft W

basis: Marshall AR 1904-05 on Stein's survey: 'remains of an important Buddhist sanctuary' on Mount Banj, identified 'with great probability'; topographical case (Songyun, Xuanzang; Chavannes) supported by the remains and the red soil; Majumdar, Petech agree; against: Cunningham ASR II pp. 154-165, XIV p. 50: Court's tope at Manikyala with an inscription read as naming the huta-murta, red soil; Rawalpindi 1883/1895 echo; Konow CII 2.1 pp. 55-57: Kharoshthi well-gift "in the Vajrastupa", year 102 (pre-Kushan), reported to Deane as from Mount Banj, probably from Stein's ancient well; does not name the jataka
